messages:
Carmen R: Hey team, one of our enterprise customers reported that several devs lost access to the project console this morning — they get a 403 on the /console route but API calls with the same API keys work. Can we triage? :frowning:
Alex W: ugh, thanks for flagging. Do we have example user emails and their SSO groups? is this after the directory sync yesterday? @Samir any idea?
Carmen R: Yep, happened ~07:10 UTC after the nightly SSO sync. Affected users are: emily@acme.com, raj@acme.com. Both are in SAML group "acme-engineers".
Samir P: I'm seeing errors in the role-sync job logs around 07:09. It looks like the sync returned groups but the mapping to project roles failed due to an unexpected claim name. Logs:
```
2026-03-15T07:09:12Z ERROR role-sync: missing claim 'groups' in identity token for tenant acme
2026-03-15T07:09:12Z WARN role-sync: skipping mapping for user emily@acme.com
```
Samir P: So SSO returned list in `memberOf` claim not `groups`. We added a fallback in the past but it didn't kick in because the config was overridden in prod last week.
Carmen R: Got it. So that's why console checks (which use token-scoped RBAC) deny them, while their API keys still work (API keys map to service-level roles).
Alex W: Can you repro? Carmen, can you paste the exact 403 response from the console request (devtools network)?
Carmen R: Here — while logged in as emily@acme.com, opening /orgs/123/projects/456/console returns 403 with body:
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "error": "permission_denied",
  "message": "You do not have permission to view this project. (project.viewer required)"
}
```
Jordan (SRE): Repro'd locally by simulating the token; token has scopes [openid email profile] but group claim is `memberOf`. Our project role-mapping config in prod only looks at `groups` — the fallback to `memberOf` was removed in 2025-11 during a cleanup PR.
Support Bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0315-0456 — tagging eng-ml and eng-platform
Samir P: Quick mitigation: I can run an onetime backfill mapping that reads `memberOf` and creates the project role bindings for affected users. That will restore console access immediately. Is acme ok with a backfill? It won't change their IdP.
Carmen R: Customer approved. Please proceed.
Samir P: Executing backfill now — script output:
```
backfill --org 123 --claim memberOf --map "acme-engineers:project.viewer"
INFO: 2 users processed, 2 role bindings created
```
Samir P: Done. Emily and Raj can now access the console. They confirmed via DM :thumbsup:
Alex W: For the long term we should: 1) add `memberOf` as an accepted claim in prod config, 2) add a small unit test on the role-sync to catch missing claim names, 3) add alerting if a full sync returns zero mapped roles for a tenant.
Jordan (SRE): I'll open a follow-up ticket to change the prod config and add the alert. Also recommending we keep a mapping doc for common IdP claim names (groups, memberOf, roles).
Carmen R: Thanks everyone. Will follow up with the customer and close the incident once they validate in 24h.
Alex W: Nice coordinated response. Uploading notes to the incident: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-0315-0456
Samir P: FYI — I'll also add a one-time cron to re-run role-sync for tenants that had >0 skipped mappings in the last 72h.
Carmen R: Closing loop: customer confirmed access restored at 07:27 UTC. Marking resolved pending config fix.
